seo_desc: 1 Christmas events for kids in SeaTac, WA, 1 free: SeaTac Winterfest at SeaTac Community Center and more.
lede: SeaTac celebrates Christmas with one big free night, SeaTac Winterfest at the SeaTac Community Center, where families meet Santa, bounce in inflatables and watch a movie with popcorn.
celebrates: The City of SeaTac's holiday celebration is Winterfest, held on an early December Friday evening at the SeaTac Community Center on 24th Avenue South. The city asks families to come in their best festive outfits for live entertainment, bouncy houses, a family movie with popcorn and photos with Santa. Every activity is free, and local food vendors sell dinner. Winterfest follows the city's earlier Holiday Tree Lighting, which brought Santa and kids' activities to the same community center in 2023 and 2024. Light rail makes it easy to add a trip to Seattle's holiday sights or Westfield Southcenter's Santa.
lastyear: In 2025 SeaTac Winterfest took place on Friday, December 5, from 5 to 8 pm at the SeaTac Community Center, 13735 24th Avenue South. The city's December newsletter listed a tree lighting at 5:15 pm, carolers, kids' crafts, Santa Claus, bouncy houses and an animated movie, all free. The year before, the city's Holiday Tree Lighting on December 6, 2024 ran from 5 to 8 pm at the same community center.
facts: SeaTac incorporated on March 14, 1989, and took its name from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, which it surrounds. The airport was dedicated on October 31, 1944. Before the city formed, the area was a string of communities including Angle Lake, Bow Lake, McMicken Heights and Riverton. In 1990 a diver found two dugout canoes, 200 to 300 years old, resting on the bottom of Angle Lake, a spring fed lake left behind by melting ice.
trains: Link light rail runs right through SeaTac, with stations at SeaTac/Airport and Angle Lake and another just north at Tukwila International Boulevard, so kids can ride a train straight to downtown Seattle and the Seattle Center Monorail. Sounder commuter trains and Amtrak Cascades stop at Tukwila Station, 7301 Longacres Way, a short drive east. For a holiday train ride, the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie runs the North Pole Limited, and the Washington State History Museum in Tacoma shows the largest permanent model railroad in the state.
train_links: The 1890 Snoqualmie Depot, weekend train rides on 5.5 miles of track and the North Pole Limited Santa train.

traditions: The city's free holiday night at the community center, with Santa photos, bouncy houses, live entertainment and a movie.

kidfact: SeaTac is named after the airport it wraps around, Seattle-Tacoma International. Put the start of Seattle and the start of Tacoma together and you get SeaTac.
faq: SeaTac Winterfest is an early December Friday evening at the SeaTac Community Center, 13735 24th Avenue South. In 2025 it ran from 5 to 8 pm on December 5, with a tree lighting at 5:15 pm. Check the City of SeaTac calendar for this year's date and lineup.

Yes. The City of SeaTac says all activities are free to participate in, including the bouncy houses, the movie with popcorn, the live entertainment and photos with Santa. Local food vendors may be on site selling food, so bring money if you plan to eat dinner there.
Can kids ride a train from SeaTac?

Yes. Link light rail stops at SeaTac/Airport and Angle Lake stations in SeaTac and at Tukwila International Boulevard just north. A ride north reaches downtown Seattle, where families can switch to the Seattle Center Monorail at Westlake Center for a second train.
Who do I contact about SeaTac holiday events?

The SeaTac Community Center front desk answers questions about Winterfest at 206-973-4680, and the city's special events team can be reached at specialevents@seatacwa.gov. The community center is at 13735 24th Avenue South, SeaTac, WA 98168, the same building where Winterfest takes place.
sources: City of SeaTac Winter Events and News
